S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

patient_info.stressor_event: Taking on a mortgage (for home, business)
patient_info.stressor: Alfred and his wife took on a business mortgage to buy a small workshop and equipment for the renewable-energy electrical company he had long imagined, a step that felt like the natural next stage of his practical ambitions. In the first weeks he became unusually expansive about the company’s future, then over seven months his energy and activity escalated into near-constant planning, job bidding, home-automation experiments, and crew changes while he slept very little and became increasingly irritable when family or apprentices questioned him. His confidence grew beyond his actual licensing timeline, and his distractibility began affecting estimates, code paperwork, and job sequencing enough that clients complained and his crew lost trust in his direction. He entered psychiatric care after his wife and a trusted church friend persuaded him to attend an urgent outpatient evaluation when the business strain and work impairment became impossible to dismiss.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: I’ll be in this big, pumped-up mood talking like our little shop is about to become the main solar outfit in town, but if my wife or one of the apprentices questions the plan I can flip and get sharp with them over nothing.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I’ve been going nonstop from job sites to bids to rewiring test panels in the workshop, starting new home-automation ideas before the last one is done because sitting still feels like wasting time.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I keep feeling like I can take on commercial jobs and train a whole crew right now, even though part of me knows my licensing and experience aren’t quite where they need to be for all that.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: For months I’ve been sleeping maybe three or four hours, then popping up before dawn feeling ready to price materials, answer emails, or sketch out another system like I had a full night’s rest.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: What finally got me here is that I can’t keep my focus on one estimate or code form anymore, because a tool noise, a text, or some new idea about the workshop pulls me off track and then jobs start getting mixed up.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: Clients have started complaining about missed details and mixed-up scheduling, and my apprentices don’t trust my direction the way they used to. At home, the mortgage and the business are turning into constant arguments because my wife feels like I’m putting everything we built at risk.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been building for about seven months, since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and equipment.
